references.text: Jesus knew all people and knew what was in man. His supernatural knowledge of Nathanael under the fig tree reflects his omniscient knowledge of human hearts, as confirmed in John 2:24-25.
The Samaritan woman recognized that Jesus was a prophet when he revealed knowledge about her private life, just as Nathanael was surprised by Jesus' supernatural knowledge in John 4:17-19.
Jesus knew from the beginning who did not believe and who would betray him. His foreknowledge of Nathanael under the fig tree is an expression of this same omniscience (John 6:64).
Peter confesses that Jesus knows all things, which confirms the supernatural knowledge Jesus showed when he saw Nathanael under the fig tree (John 21:17).

The psalmist praises God for searching and knowing man, and knowing everything – when we sit and when we stand, and knowing our thoughts from afar. Jesus' knowledge of Nathanael before Philip called him reflects this divine omniscience (Psalm 139:1-4).
God knew Jeremiah before he was formed in his mother's womb. Jesus' words that he saw Nathanael before Philip called him show a corresponding divine foreknowledge (Jeremiah 1:5).
Philip found Nathanael and told him about Jesus from Nazareth. Jesus' reference to seeing Nathanael "before Philip called you" connects directly to Philip's calling of Nathanael in John 1:45-46.

The Lord does not look at the outward appearance, but looks at the heart. Jesus' knowledge of Nathanael – that he was a true Israelite without deceit – shows that he sees people's inner character (1 Samuel 16:7).

During Solomon's peaceful reign, everyone sat under their own vine and fig tree. The fig tree was a traditional place for meditation and study of the Torah, which may shed light on what Nathanael was doing when Jesus saw him (1 Kings 4:25).
No creature is hidden from God; all things are naked and open before his eyes. Jesus' supernatural knowledge of Nathanael under the fig tree reflects this divine omniscience (Hebrews 4:13).
